Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
756 PM EDT Tue Aug 11 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 241 PM EDT Tuesday...

Have continued to increases chances for showers and embedded 
thunderstorms on Wednesday afternoon.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 245 PM EDT Tuesday...

1. Mainly dry conditions expected overnight, with renewed 
chances for showers and embedded thunderstorms Wednesday 
afternoon. 

2. More shower chances Thursday into Thursday night

3. A beautiful weekend is setting up as a dry airmass moves 
into the region. Chances for precipitation increase again late 
Sunday afternoon into Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 245 PM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Drier air continues to advect into our region 
this afternoon with gusty northwesterly winds this afternoon. 
Winds will decrease headed into the evening and overnight, with 
some fog development possible since we had a soaking rain across
much of the area in the last 24 hours. Some isolated showers 
have still managed to pop up despite drier air and some may 
track into our area from Ontario or Quebec later this afternoon 
and evening. Don't have any surface instability present to 
support stronger storms. Our region will remain in northwesterly
upper level flow through Wednesday, and additional showers with
embedded thunderstorms are expected Wednesday afternoon with a 
bit better coverage than today due to some upper level support 
with shortwave energy passing through progressive upper level 
flow. Continues to look like best chances for showers Wednesday 
will be across the northern half of our forecast area. 

KEY MESSAGE 2: A low pressure system will pass near or north of
the region later Thursday into Friday. Scattered rain with 
embedded thunderstorms can be expected with this system, with 
convective weather more uncertain and relatively limited 
compared to recent events. Still some uncertainty with timing of
features passing through, and also lacking some model 
consistency, leading to a low confidence forecast for that 
timeframe. Looks like things will kind of come through piecemeal
too, so don't think we'll see any organized storms on Thursday.


KEY MESSAGE 3: Over the weekend, much drier air moves into the 
region as high pressure pushes the low along the longwave 
pattern. Conditions will likely be quite pleasant Saturday with 
dewpoints in the 40s and 50s with temperatures generally in the 
70s. The ridge axis is projected to shift eastward Sunday and 
supports slightly warmer highs for the broader valleys with 
continued 40s and 50s dew points. Overall, these conditions are 
shaping up to be near ideal weather for outdoor activities. 
However, there is the potential (10- 40% chance of precip) for 
some showers and thunderstorms late Sunday afternoon, increasing
Sunday night and early Monday morning to 30- 60% chance as the 
next wave moves through quickly in zonal flow with a few showers
lingering on Monday. Temperatures should warm a degree or 
Monday and Tuesday as low level flow turns southwesterly.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 00Z Thursday...Northwest winds around 5kts will become
light and variable overnight with mostly clear skies as daytime
cumulus dissipate. Looking for a brief period of LIFR fog at 
MPV, SLK, and possibly EFK between 09-12Z. Otherwise, VFR 
conditions should prevail through 18Z Wednesday. Scattered 
afternoon showers and perhaps a thunderstorm is possible mid-
late Wednesday afternoon. With timing and coverage 
uncertainties, will wait for later TAF packages to specify those
details. Daylight hours Wednesday, winds increase again out of 
the west-northwest, except locally NNE at 5-8kt at KPBG.
